    Fleet clock synchronization¶

    How far apart are the scopes' clocks? A disturbance recorded on several scopes can only be lined up in time if their clocks agree. This notebook puts a bound on the clock difference between any two scopes, from repeated runs. The clocks are not made perfect; their error is measured.

    Analysis written by Claude (Anthropic); conceptualised and verified by Yatharth Bhasin.

    Protocol¶

    Acquisition: scripts/debug/fleet_clock_synchronization.py. One NTP server gives time to every scope over the wired network. Each scope runs chrony with that server as its only time source; install_requirements() sets this up once per scope. Each run then logs what chrony measures for 2 h, and the runs on all scopes overlap. The whole run is repeated at least three times (N ≥ 3). As in Lab Streaming Layer, clock offsets are measured and stored next to the data, and the error is worked out afterwards.

    Recommended: make sure the NTP server is itself well synchronized before the run.

    Running in Colab. Open this notebook with the Open in Colab button on its page. The next cell runs only in Colab: it installs what Colab lacks and asks for a .zip of your experiment folders.

    Data¶

    The run is repeated: each repeat is one folder holding one run per scope. SETS lists the folders, oldest first; below they are R1, R2, ... Runs are read with trappy-explorer's legacy reader, explorer.legacy.ExpExplorer, in legacy mode: the script writes plain numbers only, so nothing is dropped. Each run has four streams in experiment.yaml: setup (what the clock follows, at the start and the end), ntp (one row per clock update from the NTP server), pico (the Pico's clock, once a minute) and tandh.

    rich.get_console().quiet = True                           # the loader prints one line per run
exps = {r: ExpExplorer.create_superset(os.path.join(DATA, s)) for r, s in zip(REP, SETS)}
rich.get_console().quiet = False
print(exps["R1"])
print(pd.Series(SETS, index=list(exps), name="folder").to_string(), "\n")

res = []
for r, e in exps.items():
    ms = e.df_events.query("type == 'measurement_stream'")
    res.append(e.df.assign(rep=r, stream=e.df.measureid.map(dict(zip(ms.measureid, ms.name)))))
res = pd.concat(res, ignore_index=True)
res["wall"] = res.machinetime / 1e9                       # the scope's own clock, as in tracking.csv
res.columns = res.columns.str.replace("nas_", "server_")  # older column names

exp_of = {eid: e for e in exps.values() for eid in e.data}
setup = res[res.stream == "setup"].dropna(axis=1, how="all")
server_of = setup.sort_values("wall").drop_duplicates("eid").set_index("eid").server
runs = pd.DataFrame([{"rep": r, "scope": d["metadata"]["name"].split("__")[0], "eid": eid,
                      "started": d["metadata"]["created"], "server": server_of.get(eid)}
                     for r, e in exps.items() for eid, d in e.data.items()]).set_index(["rep", "scope"])
runs["hours"] = runs.eid.map(res.groupby("eid").wall.agg(lambda w: w.max() - w.min()) / 3600).round(2)
rows = res.groupby(["eid", "stream"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
runs = runs.join(rows.reindex(columns=["setup", "ntp", "pico", "tandh"], fill_value=0), on="eid").sort_index()
present = [s for s in SCOPES if s in runs.index.get_level_values("scope")]
scope_of, rep_of = runs.reset_index().set_index("eid").scope, runs.reset_index().set_index("eid").rep

    Each run folder also holds <eid>_tracking.csv: chrony's state every 10 s (chronyc tracking), taken on the same wall-clock seconds on every scope, so rows from different scopes line up. Offsets are positive when the scope's clock is ahead.

    First, check that each run was set up as intended: one time source, reached over the cable, the old time service off, and the offset sign confirmed on the scope (sign_check, expected agree). chrony's ntpdata reports the offset with the opposite sign; runs recorded before the script flipped it (test 1, 2026-11-15) show OPPOSITE, and their offsets are flipped below. differ means chrony had not yet used the last exchange.

    Maximum error¶

    chrony bounds how far the scope's clock can be from true time (UTC):

    max error = |offset| + root dispersion + root delay / 2

    Most of it is the NTP server's own distance from UTC, which is the same for every scope and cancels between two scopes. The server's own root delay (server_root_delay_s) is removed. Its root dispersion is kept: chrony reports the root dispersion of the sample it trusts most, often an older one, while the server's dispersion grows between its own updates, so the latest server_root_dispersion_s is too large to subtract (in tests 1 and 2 that gave a negative error 41-75% of the time). The error against the NTP server is then an upper bound, high by the server's root dispersion (0.3-2.2 ms in tests 1 and 2):

    error to server = |offset| + root dispersion + (root delay - server root delay) / 2
    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    ntp = res[res.stream == "ntp"].dropna(axis=1, how="all").copy()
old_sign = setup[setup.sign_check.astype(str).str.startswith("OPPOSITE")].eid.unique()
ntp.loc[ntp.eid.isin(old_sign), "offset_s"] *= -1        # recorded before the script fixed the sign
ntp = ntp.assign(scope=ntp.eid.map(scope_of), rep=ntp.eid.map(rep_of))
tr = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f"{exp_of[e].get_parent_dir(e)}/{e}_tracking.csv").assign(eid=e)
                for e in runs.eid]).sort_values("wall")
last = ntp[["eid", "wall", "server_root_delay_s"]].sort_values("wall")
last["server_root_delay_s"] = last.groupby("eid").server_root_delay_s.cummin()  # never remove too much
tr = pd.merge_asof(tr, last, on="wall", by="eid", direction="backward")
tr["err_server_s"] = (tr.clock_offset_s.abs() + tr.root_dispersion_s
                      + (tr.root_delay_s - tr.server_root_delay_s) / 2)
tr = tr.dropna(subset=["err_server_s"])                  # before the run's first clock update
tr = tr.assign(scope=tr.eid.map(scope_of), rep=tr.eid.map(rep_of))
tr["hours"] = (tr.wall - tr.groupby("rep").wall.transform("min")) / 3600   # since the repeat began
    ntp = res[res.stream == "ntp"].dropna(axis=1, how="all").copy() old_sign = setup[setup.sign_check.astype(str).str.startswith("OPPOSITE")].eid.unique() ntp.loc[ntp.eid.isin(old_sign), "offset_s"] *= -1 # recorded before the script fixed the sign ntp = ntp.assign(scope=ntp.eid.map(scope_of), rep=ntp.eid.map(rep_of)) tr = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f"{exp_of[e].get_parent_dir(e)}/{e}_tracking.csv").assign(eid=e) for e in runs.eid]).sort_values("wall") last = ntp[["eid", "wall", "server_root_delay_s"]].sort_values("wall") last["server_root_delay_s"] = last.groupby("eid").server_root_delay_s.cummin() # never remove too much tr = pd.merge_asof(tr, last, on="wall", by="eid", direction="backward") tr["err_server_s"] = (tr.clock_offset_s.abs() + tr.root_dispersion_s + (tr.root_delay_s - tr.server_root_delay_s) / 2) tr = tr.dropna(subset=["err_server_s"]) # before the run's first clock update tr = tr.assign(scope=tr.eid.map(scope_of), rep=tr.eid.map(rep_of)) tr["hours"] = (tr.wall - tr.groupby("rep").wall.transform("min")) / 3600 # since the repeat began

The dashed line is the acceptable error for one scope, half of ACCEPT_MS: two scopes that both stay below it differ by less than ACCEPT_MS. A slow ramp means the scope lost its NTP server for a while; a narrow peak is one slow network exchange.

    Scope to scope¶

    At every 10 s tick, two scopes' clocks differ by at most the sum of their errors against the NTP server. Over the time all runs of a repeat overlap, each map shows the value this bound stays below 99% of the time, one map per repeat. This holds when every server address belongs to the same NTP server, as here; otherwise compare against UTC instead.

    The colour scale runs from 0 to the acceptance limit (ACCEPT_MS). The differences between pairs are not a property of the scopes: they do not repeat from one repeat to the next. What holds for the fleet is the fleet bound, in the table below the maps: at each tick, any two scopes differ by at most the sum of the two largest errors at that tick; the fleet bound is its 99th percentile over the repeat.

    The Pico's clock¶

    Each scope's Pico keeps its own clock, and nothing synchronizes it. The run reads it once a minute over the serial link: as found for the first 5 min, then sets it once to the scope's time (UTC) and follows it. Each reading is a request and reply timed to the moment the Pico's seconds tick over, with an error of a few ms (error_s). This is for information and is not part of the acceptance. A Pico keeps its clock until it loses power, so it is found either as set by an earlier run, or restarted at 2021-01-01 (about -1.85e8 s).

    As found: the board, whether its clock counts fractions of a second, and how far its clock was off at the start of each repeat (found_s, + = ahead).

    Results¶

    Per run: one row per repeat and scope, also written next to each run's data (analysis/fleet_clock_synchronization.yaml). err_*_ms is the error against the NTP server (the upper bound above); utc_p99_ms is chrony's own bound against UTC; longest_gap_s is the longest time between two clock updates; accepted: the scope's own error stays below ACCEPT_MS / 2 for 99% of the run. pico_*: how far off the Pico's clock was as found (s, + = ahead), its offset right after it was set (ms), its drift (ppm) and how far it moved after the set (ms). fleet_bound_ms is the repeat's fleet bound.

    Acceptance¶

    The fleet passes when the fleet bound, how far apart any two scopes' clocks can be for 99% of a repeat, stays below ACCEPT_MS = 4 ms in every repeat. 4 ms is a tenth of one frame at 25 fps, so a disturbance seen on two scopes falls in the same frame. Each scope's own share is ACCEPT_MS / 2: the dashed line in the first figure, and accepted in the results.

    Persistent records¶

    This calibration writes 0 records to the scope. Its set-up step, install_requirements(), does change the scope's time service: chrony replaces systemd-timesyncd, with the NTP server as its only source. The run also sets each Pico's clock to UTC once; the Pico loses that setting when it loses power.
